ctx.x: And Hal Howard, was booking it, said, 'Don't worry about it. He's doing something. This isn't going to cost you anything.' But this guy was aghast, you know. He said, 'My God.' I said, 'Don't worry. This is not going to cost you anything,' because I was getting this band together. And as I found guys -- I knew I didn't have time to go through the process, you know, of building a band and keep working. I had to keep adding them and then as I found them, and we

came up with a pretty fair band. Johnny Markham playing drums and a good tenor saxophone player from up north whose name escapes me. And Ray was there and it was his generalship in the trumpet section, and he took some of the guys that were there and got them together pretty good. Al Porsino joined the band. And by the time we got to New York it was a pretty respectable band. And we went in and played Bop City and that's when I pulled my thing. I got in a bind with a wife of mine, and on top of that I had a boy…

and I stopped the band. I said, "I've been wanting to do this all my life. You can all go fuck yourselves." And I took my soprano and I broke it over my knee and walked out of the club, downstairs, and got in a taxicab and went to the airport and took a plane to California. Now, that is exactly what happened.
